queued_query: Asked {{sn}} for {{what}}: {{count}} command(s) on the queue. The device collects one per poll, so this takes roughly {{seconds}} seconds, and nothing has been read yet — watch Commands for the outcome.{{extra}}
queued_query_reused: Asked {{sn}} for {{what}}: {{count}} command(s) on the queue ({{reused}} already waiting from an earlier click). The device collects one per poll, so this takes roughly {{seconds}} seconds, and nothing has been read yet — watch Commands for the outcome.{{extra}}

query.attendance_excluded: Attendance is not included — these terminals push punches up by themselves.

queued_control: Queued: {{what}}. This terminal is not dialled — it collects commands when it next polls, about every 10 seconds, and nothing has happened yet. Watch Commands for the outcome.{{extra}}

control.refresh_params: asked the terminal to re-send its parameters
control.reused: (an identical request was already waiting, so this reuses it rather than costing another poll cycle.)
control.unlock_warning: THIS IS NOT AN IMMEDIATE UNLOCK: the door opens when the terminal next polls, usually within about 10 seconds. If it has not collected the command within {{ttl}} seconds the command is cancelled and the door will NOT open later.
control.restart_offline: It will go offline briefly once it collects this, and reconnect by itself.
control.clear_records: clear the access-control records held on the terminal
control.clear_records_note: Nothing has been deleted yet, and nothing already synced to this database is affected either way.

command_cancelled_sent: This command was already delivered to the device at least once — cancelling only removes our record of owing it. The device may already have collected and acted on it; nothing was recalled.
command_cancelled_sent_revocation: This command was already delivered to the device at least once — cancelling only removes our record of owing it. The device may already have collected and acted on it; nothing was recalled. That person's access may already be gone — check the terminal directly if this needs to be certain.
command_cancelled_pending: Cancelled before delivery. This command was never sent to the device.
retry_refused: Requeued. The device refused this with Return={{return_code}} last time — unless something changed at the device, it will very likely refuse again the same way.
retry_unconfirmed: Requeued. The device answered Return={{return_code}} last time, which this system cannot read as either success or refusal — so it may already have worked. Sending it again is safe; it is not a retry of a known failure.
retry_requeued: Requeued as a new command. The previous attempt was never acknowledged; this one starts its own delivery attempts from zero.
info_last_known: Last known values, reported by the terminal itself — not a live reading. An access-control terminal cannot be dialled for this; it sends its parameters when it registers and whenever they change. Use Refresh to ask it again, which is queued and answers on its next poll.
info_none_yet: This terminal has not sent its parameters yet, so there is nothing to show. They arrive when it registers; Refresh asks for them now, which is queued and answers on its next poll.
bulk_queued: Queued {{commands}} commands for {{people}} people. At one command per poll this takes roughly {{seconds}} seconds to drain, and nothing is delivered until the device collects it.
push_queued: Queued {{count}} commands for {{sn}}. The device collects them on its next poll (about 10 seconds) and acknowledges afterwards — this is not delivered yet.
revoke_withdrawn: This person was never confirmed on {{sn}}; the {{count}} command(s) still waiting to put them there have been withdrawn. Nothing was sent to the device.
revoke_queued: Access revoked in the system — NOT yet confirmed at the door. {{sn}} collects one command per poll (about 10 seconds) and confirms afterwards; until it does, this person can still open that door. If the terminal is offline the revocation waits, and stays visible as outstanding.
revoke_removed: Removed from {{sn}}. The device confirmed it.
revocation_cancelled: Revocation cancelled. {{user_id}} keeps their access to {{sn}} — if they were already confirmed on it, nothing about the device changed at any point.
templates_queued: Queued {{count}} commands for {{sn}}: {{templates}} template(s). At one command per poll this takes roughly {{seconds}} seconds, and nothing is delivered until the device collects it — this is not delivered yet.
templates_queued_behind: Queued {{count}} commands for {{sn}}: {{templates}} template(s) behind the person's user record and door permission, which this terminal has not confirmed yet. At one command per poll this takes roughly {{seconds}} seconds, and nothing is delivered until the device collects it — this is not delivered yet.
enroll_started: Enrollment started — the person must scan their finger on the device
employee_deleted: {{user_id}} removed from the system. Attendance history is kept — those rows are historical fact and already reached the HRM. If a device still holds this PIN, a future sync will re-create the employee record from what the terminal reports; that is correct behaviour, not a bug.
